hero.description: Brent crude remains above $100 a barrel as attacks on shipping around the Strait of Hormuz intensify, raising fresh concerns about inflation, fuel costs and global economic growth.

featured.title: Brent Holds Above $100 as Shipping Disruption Deepens
featured.content: Brent crude remained above $100 a barrel on Thursday as the conflict involving the United States and Iran continued to disrupt shipping around the Strait of Hormuz. Brent was around $101.10 in early trading, while U.S. West Texas Intermediate was about $96.24. Prices have risen almost 30% from early-August lows. The Strait normally carries roughly one-fifth of global oil and gas supplies, making prolonged disruption a major risk for fuel prices, transport costs and inflation worldwide.

articles.title: Oil Holds Above $100 as Hormuz Disruption Continues
articles.content: Brent crude remained above $100 a barrel on Thursday as attacks on shipping intensified. Reuters reported Brent around $101.10 and WTI around $96.24 in early trading. Brent has risen nearly 30% from its early-August lows as traders assess the possibility of prolonged disruption to Persian Gulf energy supplies.
articles.imageQuery: Brent crude oil barrels global energy market

articles.title: Strait of Hormuz Remains at Centre of Energy Crisis
articles.content: The Strait of Hormuz normally carries roughly one-fifth of global oil and gas supplies. Flows have fallen sharply during the conflict, while uncertainty over tanker movements and alternative export routes is adding a significant risk premium to oil prices.
articles.imageQuery: Strait of Hormuz oil tankers aerial

articles.title: Iran Claims Attacks on 10 Ships
articles.content: Iran says it attacked 10 ships near the Strait of Hormuz after the United States sank five Iranian oil tankers. At least one seafarer has reportedly died and another remains missing. The conflicting claims surrounding the maritime attacks remain part of a rapidly developing military situation.
articles.imageQuery: Iran Strait of Hormuz military oil tanker

articles.title: Trump Warns Iran Over Pickaxe Mountain
articles.content: President Donald Trump warned Iran against increased activity at Pickaxe Mountain, a fortified site containing deeply buried tunnel complexes near the damaged Natanz uranium-enrichment facility. Trump said the United States could respond militarily if Iran took what Washington regarded as provocative action. The situation remains developing and individual military claims require careful verification.
articles.imageQuery: Donald Trump Iran nuclear facility Middle East

articles.title: Houthi Attacks Threaten Additional Energy Routes
articles.content: Iran-aligned Houthi forces have increased attacks on Saudi Arabia, adding another layer of risk to Gulf energy infrastructure and shipping routes. The possibility of disruption spreading beyond the Strait of Hormuz has increased anxiety in global energy markets.
articles.imageQuery: Saudi Arabia oil energy infrastructure Yemen Houthis

articles.title: Dangote Warns Global Fuel Shortages Could Continue
articles.content: Dangote Refinery says global fuel shortages could remain tight even after the current Iran conflict eventually ends. The company points to damage to refining infrastructure in the Middle East and Russia, high refinery utilisation and depleted fuel inventories. Dangote reported a $1.82bn profit in the first half of 2026 compared with a $476m loss a year earlier.

articles.title: Dangote Plans $14.3bn Nigerian Refinery Expansion
articles.content: Dangote plans to invest about $14.3bn to double the refinery's capacity from around 700,000 barrels per day to approximately 1.4 million barrels per day by 2029. The planned IPO is expected to raise about ₦2.15tn, or approximately $1.63bn, with the offer scheduled from September 14 to October 13.

articles.title: Dangote Plans Major Refinery Project in Kenya
articles.content: Dangote Group is planning a proposed 700,000-barrel-per-day refinery in Lamu, Kenya, estimated to cost between $15bn and $16bn. Construction could begin later this month, with completion targeted around 2030. A major challenge is securing sufficient crude because Kenya currently has no commercial crude production.

articles.title: Kenya Refinery Could Reshape East African Fuel Supply
articles.content: If successfully financed and completed, the proposed Lamu refinery could significantly increase refining capacity in East Africa and reduce dependence on imported refined petroleum products. However, crude supply, infrastructure, financing and transport remain major challenges.

articles.title: Nepal Seeks $5bn for First Phase of Flood Recovery
articles.content: Nepal plans to ask wealthy countries and international agencies to help fund about $5bn needed for the first phase of rebuilding after catastrophic flooding triggered by the collapse of a Himalayan glacier. Officials say the initial funding requirement covers the first five months of recovery and will be presented to institutions including the World Bank and Asian Development Bank.

articles.title: Nepal Flood Disaster Leaves Thousands Missing
articles.content: At least 1,300 people have been confirmed dead and more than 5,300 remain missing across Nepal and China's Tibet region following the catastrophic late-August disaster. More than 12 hydropower plants and major roads, bridges, homes and trade routes were also damaged or destroyed.

articles.title: Asian Stocks Fall as Oil Stays Above $100
articles.content: Asian shares declined on Thursday as investors reacted to escalating Middle East tensions and oil prices above $100. The MSCI Asia-Pacific index fell about 1%, while Japan's Nikkei and South Korea's KOSPI also dropped more than 1%. Investors are watching inflation data and central-bank decisions closely.

articles.title: US Treasury Yields Remain Near 2023 Highs
articles.content: The U.S. 10-year Treasury yield remained around 4.84%, close to its highest level since 2023. Rising oil prices are increasing fears that inflation could remain elevated, making the outlook for interest rates more uncertain.

articles.title: ECB Faces Fresh Inflation Pressure
articles.content: The European Central Bank is facing a renewed inflation challenge as higher energy prices linked to the Middle East conflict feed into transport, manufacturing and household costs. Markets expect the ECB to raise interest rates again, while investors will watch its guidance for clues about future policy.

articles.title: Yen Remains Strong as BOJ Rate Hike Expectations Rise
articles.content: The Japanese yen remains close to a seven-month high against the dollar. It was around 153.63 per dollar after strengthening about 4% during September. Investors increasingly expect the Bank of Japan to raise interest rates, with its communication next week likely to be closely watched.

articles.title: Energy Shock Raises Questions for Global Technology Industry
articles.content: Higher energy prices are adding to operating costs for data centres, manufacturers and other energy-intensive technology businesses. Investors are therefore assessing whether prolonged energy inflation could affect technology-sector margins and investment plans.

morningSummary.title: 🌍 RadiantWaves Morning News & Update
morningSummary.content: Good morning. The global economy begins Thursday under renewed pressure as Brent crude remains above $100 a barrel and shipping disruption around the Strait of Hormuz continues. The escalation is also affecting inflation expectations, financial markets and central-bank decisions. In Africa, Dangote is pursuing major refinery expansion in Nigeria and a proposed refinery in Kenya, while Nepal is seeking $5bn for the first phase of recovery from a catastrophic Himalayan flood disaster.

bigQuestion: With oil now above $100 a barrel, what should governments prioritise most — protecting consumers from rising costs, increasing domestic energy production, or accelerating the transition to alternative energy?
